title: Protocol for assessing real-time changes in mitochondrial morphology, fission and fusion events in live cells using confocal microscopy
protocol: Transfect the cells with CellLight™ Mitochondria-RFP, BacMan 2.0 following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 3 μL of BacMan 2.0 reagent per 104 cells directly in the complete medium and incubate O.N. at 37°C.
Check the transfection efficiency using a confocal microscope.
Image the transfected cells to observe well-defined and bright mitochondria.
Acquire images using a white-light supercontinuum laser set at 0.2% intensity.
Set the excitation wavelength to 555 nm and emission wavelength to 584 nm collected using a Hyd detector.
Set scanning format to 512 x 512.
Set Pinhole Unit: AU, Airy 1.
Set pixel size to 72.22 nm x 72.22 nm.
Automatically calculate the optical section thickness by software.
Capture a z-stack of 30-40 slices for each XYZT with a step size of 0.12 μm.
Set scanning speed to 8000 Hz.
Turn on Bidirectional X to increase imaging speed.
Adjust Phase X if there is image distortion.
Perform time-lapse imaging for 2 minutes with a 3-second interval.
Adjust the zoom to 4× to sample the image at the optimum density/Nyquist Rate.
Acquire movies with different lengths (e.g., 2, 3, and 4 minutes) when testing a new cell line.
Check the stability of cells in the selected time frame for optimization.
Use a short acquisition time (2 minutes) for cancer cell lines that move.
Adjust intervals between acquisitions based on cell line dynamics.
Acquire images every 3 seconds for dynamic cell lines with active mitochondria.
Extend the interval if analysis shows no changes in mitochondrial volume over time.
Acquire the whole cell in the z dimension using a confocal microscope.
Select cells with similar fluorescence intensity for acquisition.
Choose cells with well-defined mitochondria for analysis.
Acquire at least 10 cells for each condition.
Select small enough cells or parts of large cells to fit within the field of view.
Choose peripheral areas of the cell where mitochondria are spread out.
Transfer file to a computer workstation.
Open Huygens professional software.
Deconvolve images using the Huygens professional software to improve resolution and quality.
Decrease noise in the recorded images during deconvolution process.
Right click on the selected image in Leica Las X software.
Select export → to Huygens Professional.
Open the Edit Microscope Parameters window from the main toolbar or thumbnail toolbar in Huygens professional software.
Use the Leica image properties report to check the metadata imported with the image file.
Update the Embedding med. refractive index: 1.38.
Update the Excitation wavelength (555 nm) and Emission wavelength (584 nm).
Click on the Set all verified button.
Save the Image Properties by clicking the Accept button.
Start the deconvolution process.
Open Deconvolution Wizard.
Enter Deconvolution Wizard.
Select the Point Spread Function (P.S.F.) setting in the software.
Crop the image if necessary to reduce the area that needs deconvolution.
Inspect the image histogram to check for saturation or clipping.
Identify sharp peaks at the left or rightmost sides as an indication of clipping.
Look for a significant amount of black level, which appears as a gap on the left side of the histogram.
Estimate the background value of the image automatically or manually.
Note that in this protocol, the background is estimated automatically.
Select an area in/near the object to estimate background.
Click the Auto button for automatic estimation.
Click the Accept button to confirm the estimated background.
Set up deconvolution parameters based on previous stage results.
Adjust maximum iterations if necessary to achieve desired image quality.
Control signal to noise ratio to adjust image sharpness.
Select resume to return to the stage where the deconvolution parameters can be entered.
Accept the result by pressing ‘All done’.
Save the template to retain used settings for future application.
Close the deconvolution process by pressing ‘Done’.
Export images to the main window in Hyugens professional.
Right click on the image and select ‘Export’.
Choose ‘push/pull’ from the export options.
Confirm that the image is sent to the export list.
Export multiple images at the same time if needed.
Quantify the volume of each mitochondrion using Leica LAS X software.
Investigate variation in mitochondrial volume over time using 3D images.
Ensure images are well-defined and allow discrimination of every single mitochondrion as a single object.
Open the image of interest using the Leica L.A.S. X software.
Click on the 3D button to start the analysis.
Select the image of interest for analysis.
Click on the ‘append’ button to append the selected image to the software.
Set the threshold by hand using the same parameters for all images in one experiment.
Separate objects after setting the threshold.
Draw the region of interest manually, including around 10–20 mitochondria.
Adjust the threshold (Processing Sequence panel) using the same parameters for all images in a single experiment.
Select objects tool in Leica Las X software.
Set to split objects and click on ‘No filters’.
Adjust the object size to 1 μm.
Select a region containing a limited number (10–20) of well-resolved mitochondria.
Check that mitochondria within the region of interest do not move out of it or that mitochondria initially excluded from that region do not become included over time.
Move the time bar to observe the movement of mitochondria in the selected area.
Select 'Click on select Regions' to exclude objects outside the region of interest from analysis.
Consider yellow objects for analysis and exclude light green objects.
Choose a region where mitochondria are not too dense to ensure they are recognized as separate objects by the software.
Measure the volume of each mitochondrion for every time frame.
Obtain an excel file displaying the volume of all objects within the R.O.I. at each time point.
Measure frame point 6 of Processing Sequence panel in Leica Las X software.
Select the smallest object [voxel] as 6 in the bottom panel (7. Measurements).
Unflag 'track particle'.
The software analyzes the volume of each single mitochondrion over time.
Click on ‘Histogram’ point 9 of Processing Sequence panel.
Generate a histogram of the analyzed objects with different colors associated to different volumes.
Click on ‘Create Report’, point 10 of the Processing Sequence panel.
Export an excel file containing different tabs/sheets.
Select the 'Feature Details' sheet in the exported excel file.
Copy the ‘Time Index’ and the ‘Volume’ columns from the 'Feature Details' sheet.
Paste the copied columns into a new excel file.
Repeat the process for at least 3 different regions of interest (R.O.I.) for each cell.
Measure the average volume of mitochondria at each time point.
Calculate the variation in mitochondrial volume over time as fold increase or decrease from the initial volume.
Prepare an excel file reporting the volume of mitochondria for each time point in separate columns.
Calculate the average mitochondrial volume for each time point.
Divide the average volume at T1 by the volume at T0 to calculate the variation.
Divide the average volume at T2 by the volume at T1 to calculate the variation.
Repeat the procedure for all subsequent time points.
Prepare a new excel table with the calculated volume variations over time for each R.O.I.
Set up a threshold where a fold increase higher than 1.3 represents a fusion event.
Set up a threshold where a fold decrease lower than 0.7 represents a fission event.
